subject: dedal status - learned scoring wins, the 512 limit hurts
body:
Status for the May 29 milestone, a couple of days early.

Homology reproduction was clean back in April. On our own event streams, learned alignment beats fixed-cost edit distance by a distance: 0.81 vs 0.62 on our pair-matching task. The contextual gap penalties are doing the work - our streams have long runs of retries that a fixed gap-extend penalty punishes indiscriminately, and the learned parameters figure out that a long homogeneous gap is cheap while a short heterogeneous one is expensive. That's a genuinely nice result.

The cost is the 512 limit. Median stream is 1,900 events, so we window at 480 with 32-event overlap and stitch. Stitching is where the errors live - about 70% of our remaining failures are pairs whose true alignment crosses a window boundary. Memory is also tight because of the 512x512x9 path tensor, so we can't just widen the window.

Anders, worth deciding whether we invest in a hierarchical scheme or accept the ceiling.

Katya
